distros.name: Linux Mint
distros.description: Looks and feels like Windows. Everything works right after install.
distros.release: Fixed, a new version every 2 years
pros: Familiar layout if you come from Windows
cons: Software is a bit older than on rolling distros
Wayland support is still experimental
distros.highlight: Feels like Windows from the first minute

distros.name: Ubuntu
distros.description: The most popular Linux. You can find help for any problem.
pros: Most Linux guides are written for it
cons: Uses Snap packages by default
GNOME needs extensions to look like Windows
distros.highlight: The distro most guides are written for

distros.name: Pop!_OS
distros.description: Based on Ubuntu, with NVIDIA drivers ready and built-in tiling.
cons: The COSMIC desktop is still young
Fewer ready themes than GNOME or KDE
distros.highlight: Tiling built into a normal desktop

distros.name: Debian
distros.description: Very stable. The software is older, but it almost never breaks.
pros: One of the biggest package archives
Run by the community, not a company
cons: Older software in the stable version
The installer asks more questions
distros.highlight: The rock that many distros are built on

distros.name: Fedora
distros.description: New software and a clean desktop. Great for programming.
pros: New software that is tested first
cons: Codecs and NVIDIA drivers need RPM Fusion
You upgrade to a new version every year

distros.name: openSUSE Tumbleweed
distros.description: Always up to date, with automatic snapshots if an update fails.
pros: Rolling, but every update is tested first
Snapshots let you undo a bad update
cons: Smaller community than Ubuntu or Arch
Codecs need the Packman repo

distros.name: Manjaro
distros.description: Based on Arch, with a graphical installer and ready-made desktops.
cons: Packages arrive later than on Arch
Arch guides do not always match
distros.highlight: Arch, with a pause before updates

distros.name: EndeavourOS
distros.description: Almost pure Arch with an easy installer. Great for ricing.
cons: You fix problems in the terminal
Few graphical tools

distros.name: Arch Linux
distros.description: You build the system piece by piece. The best wiki in the Linux world.
pros: The Arch Wiki is the best Linux manual
The AUR has almost every program
cons: You build the system yourself
It needs regular care
distros.highlight: You build it yourself, piece by piece

distros.name: Kubuntu
distros.description: Ubuntu with the KDE Plasma desktop, which you can change in many ways.
pros: Looks like Windows from the start
cons: Uses Snap like Ubuntu
So many settings can feel like a lot

distros.name: Zorin OS
distros.description: Based on Ubuntu, with a layout that looks like Windows or macOS.
pros: Layouts that look like Windows or macOS
Helps you run some Windows apps
cons: Some layouts need the paid Pro edition
New versions come later than Ubuntu

distros.name: elementary OS
distros.forWho: People who like a clean macOS look
distros.description: A simple and beautiful desktop with its own apps and store.
cons: Less customizable than other desktops
The download page asks for a payment (you can enter 0)

distros.name: LMDE
distros.description: Linux Mint built on Debian instead of Ubuntu.
pros: The Mint look on a Debian base
cons: Fewer users than the main Mint
Older drivers than Ubuntu based Mint

distros.name: MX Linux
distros.description: A light Debian based system with many handy tools.
pros: Live USB that can save your files
cons: The default look is a bit old
Starts with sysVinit by default (systemd is optional)
distros.highlight: Gives old laptops a second life

distros.name: Kali Linux
distros.description: Debian based, comes with hundreds of security tools.
pros: Great for networking and security classes
Can run from a USB stick
cons: Not made for daily use
Use the tools only on networks you own

distros.name: Nobara
distros.description: Fedora with gaming drivers and codecs already set up.
cons: Made by a small team
Differs from Fedora in some places

distros.name: Rocky Linux
distros.description: A free system that is built to be the same as Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
distros.basedOn: Compatible with Red Hat Enterprise Linux
distros.release: Point releases with about 10 years of support
pros: Learn the same system that companies use
cons: Old software for a desktop
Fewer desktop apps

distros.name: AlmaLinux
distros.description: A free Red Hat compatible system with long support.
distros.basedOn: Compatible with Red Hat Enterprise Linux
distros.release: Point releases with about 10 years of support
cons: Old software for a desktop
Fewer desktop apps

distros.name: openSUSE Leap
distros.forWho: People who want stable and predictable
distros.description: The stable version of openSUSE, updated in big steps.
distros.release: A new point release every year
cons: Older software
Smaller community

distros.name: Garuda Linux
distros.forWho: Gamers and people who want a pretty Arch
distros.description: Arch with a colorful desktop and snapshots, ready after install.
cons: Heavy on old computers
Many effects you may want to turn off
distros.highlight: A gaming Arch with wow effects

distros.name: CachyOS
distros.description: Arch with a fast kernel and packages built for new processors.
pros: Packages and kernels tuned for speed
Many desktops to pick at install
cons: Not made for complete beginners
Rolling updates need attention

distros.name: Omarchy
distros.forWho: Developers who want a ready Hyprland
distros.description: Arch Linux with a complete Hyprland desktop, themes and apps set up for you.
pros: A beautiful Hyprland setup in minutes
Keyboard first, very fast to use
Many themes you switch with one key
cons: Opinionated: many choices are made for you
You need to learn the keyboard shortcuts
distros.highlight: A finished Hyprland setup in minutes

packages.name: Hyprland
packages.description: A modern tiling window manager for Wayland, with animations and rounded corners.
packages.why: The most popular choice for ricing: it looks great and everything is set in one config file.
packages.highlight: Smooth animations and blur on Wayland

packages.name: Sway
packages.description: A simple and stable tiling window manager for Wayland.
packages.why: It works on almost every distro, so it is a calm first step into tiling.
packages.highlight: i3 config, but on Wayland

packages.name: BSPWM
packages.description: A tiling window manager for X11, controlled with shell commands.
packages.why: Good for older laptops and for people who like to script everything.
packages.highlight: Controlled only by shell commands

packages.name: Waybar
packages.description: The status bar at the top of the screen, for Wayland.
packages.why: Shows the clock, battery, Wi-Fi and workspaces. You style it with CSS, like a web page.
packages.highlight: Every module styled with CSS

packages.name: Polybar
packages.description: A status bar for X11 window managers.
packages.why: The classic bar for BSPWM and i3 setups.
packages.highlight: The classic bar for X11 rices

packages.name: Rofi
packages.description: An app launcher: press a key, type a name, open the app.
packages.why: A tiling window manager has no start menu. Rofi is the start menu.
packages.highlight: Launcher, window switcher and menus in one

packages.name: Wofi
packages.description: A small app launcher made for Wayland.
packages.why: A light alternative to Rofi for Hyprland and Sway.
packages.highlight: Simple launcher made for Wayland

packages.name: Dunst
packages.description: Shows small notification pop-ups.
packages.why: Without it you never see messages like 'battery low' in a tiling setup.
packages.highlight: Notifications you style with one file

packages.name: Feh
packages.description: An image viewer that can also set your wallpaper.
packages.why: The easiest way to put a wallpaper on an X11 desktop.
packages.highlight: Image viewer and wallpaper setter in one

packages.name: Zsh
packages.description: A shell: the program that reads the commands you type.
packages.why: Better autocomplete than Bash and lots of themes (Oh My Zsh).
packages.highlight: Plugins and themes with Oh My Zsh

packages.name: Fish
packages.description: A friendly shell that suggests commands while you type.
packages.why: Perfect for beginners: it is helpful with zero configuration.
packages.highlight: Suggests commands while you type

packages.name: Alacritty
packages.description: A fast terminal that uses your graphics card.
packages.why: Simple, fast and configured with a single text file.
packages.highlight: Drawn by the GPU, almost no delay

packages.name: Kitty
packages.description: A fast terminal with tabs, splits and image previews.
packages.why: Very popular in riced setups, with hundreds of ready-made themes.
packages.highlight: Shows images inside the terminal

packages.name: Foot
packages.description: A tiny and very fast terminal for Wayland.
packages.why: Starts instantly and uses almost no memory.
packages.highlight: Tiny and very fast on Wayland

packages.name: Tmux
packages.description: Splits one terminal into many panes and keeps your work open.
packages.why: Very useful when you work on a server over SSH.
packages.highlight: Your terminal keeps running after you leave

packages.name: Btop
packages.description: Shows CPU, memory, disk and running programs.
packages.why: It is the Linux Task Manager, only prettier.
packages.highlight: Graphs for CPU, memory, disk and network

packages.name: Fastfetch
packages.description: Prints your distro logo and system info in the terminal.
packages.why: The screenshot every ricer posts. Also a quick way to see your hardware.
packages.highlight: System info and a logo in one second

packages.name: Fzf
packages.description: Fuzzy search for files and for your command history.
packages.why: Press Ctrl+R and find any old command in one second.
packages.highlight: Fuzzy search for files and history

packages.name: Ripgrep
packages.description: Searches text inside files, very fast.
packages.why: A faster and simpler grep.
packages.highlight: Searches a whole project in milliseconds

packages.name: Neovim
packages.description: A text editor that runs inside the terminal.
packages.why: Fast, works everywhere and can grow into a full code editor.
packages.highlight: Editor you extend with Lua plugins

packages.name: VLC
packages.description: Plays almost any video or audio file.
packages.why: Opens the files that other players refuse to open.
packages.highlight: Plays almost every file, no codecs needed

packages.name: MPV
packages.description: A minimal video player controlled from the keyboard.
packages.why: Light and fits perfectly in a tiling setup.
packages.highlight: Minimal player, controlled by keys

packages.name: GIMP
packages.description: An image editor, a free alternative to Photoshop.
packages.why: Edit photos or make your own wallpapers.
packages.highlight: Layers, masks and filters for photos

packages.name: OBS Studio
packages.description: Records or streams your screen.
packages.why: Record your desktop to show off your rice.
packages.highlight: Record and stream with scenes

packages.name: Thunar
packages.description: A light file manager with windows and icons.
packages.why: Tiling window managers come without a file manager. Thunar is fast and simple.
packages.highlight: Light file manager with bulk rename

packages.name: Yazi
packages.description: A file manager inside the terminal, with image previews.
packages.why: Move through your files with the keyboard, very fast.
packages.highlight: Terminal file manager with image previews

packages.name: Git
packages.description: Saves the history of your files and talks to GitHub.
packages.why: Almost every dotfiles repo and coding project needs it.
packages.highlight: Every change saved and undoable

packages.name: Curl
packages.description: Downloads files from the internet, from the terminal.
packages.why: Many install guides start with a curl command.
packages.highlight: Talk to any URL or API from the terminal

packages.name: Flatpak
packages.description: A second app store that works on every distro.
packages.why: Gets you apps like Spotify or Discord even when your distro does not have them.
packages.highlight: Apps that run the same on every distro

packages.name: Timeshift
packages.description: Takes snapshots of your system so you can go back in time.
packages.why: If an update breaks something, you restore yesterday's system in minutes.
packages.highlight: Undo a broken update in two clicks

packages.name: UFW
packages.description: A simple firewall.
packages.why: One command (sudo ufw enable) blocks unwanted connections.
packages.highlight: A firewall with one simple command

packages.name: i3
packages.description: A tiling window manager for X11 that you set up with one plain text file.
packages.why: The classic first tiling window manager, with years of guides and example configs to copy.
packages.highlight: The most copied tiling config ever

packages.name: Awesome
packages.description: A tiling window manager for X11 that you configure in the Lua language.
packages.why: Good if you want to program your own desktop and add widgets.
packages.highlight: The desktop is a Lua program

packages.name: Openbox
packages.description: A very light floating window manager for X11, easy to theme.
packages.why: Runs fast on old laptops and uses almost no memory.
packages.highlight: Right click the desktop to get the menu

packages.name: xmonad
packages.description: A tiling window manager for X11, written and configured in Haskell.
packages.why: A good pick if you like functional programming and want a very stable desktop.
packages.highlight: Configured in Haskell, never crashes

packages.name: DWM
packages.description: A tiny tiling window manager from suckless that you change by editing its C code.
packages.why: It teaches you how a window manager works, but it is not for beginners.
packages.highlight: About 2000 lines of C, nothing more

packages.name: Herbstluftwm
packages.description: A manual tiling window manager for X11, configured with shell commands.
packages.why: Simple to learn and easy to script, with a clear config file.
packages.highlight: You split the screen by hand

packages.name: Qtile
packages.description: A tiling window manager written in Python that works on X11 and Wayland.
packages.why: If you know Python, you can configure it with code you already understand.
packages.highlight: Configured in Python

packages.name: Tint2
packages.description: A simple panel and taskbar for X11 window managers like Openbox.
packages.why: Gives a light window manager a bar with a clock and the open windows.
packages.highlight: Light taskbar for Openbox

packages.name: Fuzzel
packages.description: An app launcher for Wayland, small and fast.
packages.why: A lighter alternative to Wofi that looks clean with Hyprland and Sway.
packages.highlight: Fast launcher with icons for Wayland

packages.name: Dmenu
packages.description: A very small launcher for X11 that shows a text list at the top of the screen.
packages.why: It is used with dwm and i3, and many scripts use it for menus.
packages.highlight: A menu that reads a list and returns a choice

packages.name: Mako
packages.description: A light notification daemon for Wayland.
packages.why: It shows your notifications on Sway and Hyprland and is easy to restyle.
packages.highlight: Light notifications for Wayland

packages.name: Swaylock
packages.description: A screen locker for Wayland compositors.
packages.why: Locks the screen when you leave the computer, and works with Sway and others.
packages.highlight: Lock screen with colors and images

packages.name: Swayidle
packages.description: Runs a command when the computer is idle, for example to lock the screen.
packages.why: Together with Swaylock it locks the screen after a few minutes.
packages.highlight: Lock or sleep after you stop using the PC

packages.name: Swaybg
packages.description: Shows a wallpaper on Wayland.
packages.why: Wayland has no wallpaper tool by default, so you need one like this.
packages.highlight: The simplest wallpaper for Wayland

packages.name: Hyprpaper
packages.description: A fast wallpaper tool made for Hyprland.
packages.why: It reads its settings from a simple file next to your Hyprland config.
packages.highlight: Fast wallpaper made by the Hyprland team

packages.name: Hyprlock
packages.description: The screen locker made by the Hyprland team, with blur and custom widgets.
packages.why: It matches the look of Hyprland and is easy to theme.
packages.highlight: Lock screen with blur and widgets

packages.name: Hypridle
packages.description: The idle daemon of Hyprland: lock the screen or turn off the display after a while.
packages.why: It saves battery and works together with Hyprlock.
packages.highlight: Turns the screen off when idle

packages.name: Swww
packages.description: A wallpaper daemon for Wayland with smooth animated transitions.
packages.why: Nice if you want the wallpaper to change with an animation.
packages.highlight: Wallpapers that change with an animation

packages.name: Grim
packages.description: A screenshot tool for Wayland.
packages.why: Use it with Slurp to take a screenshot of a part of the screen.
packages.highlight: Screenshots on Wayland

packages.name: Slurp
packages.description: Lets you select a region of the screen on Wayland.
packages.why: Slurp gives the region and Grim takes the picture.
packages.highlight: Select any part of the screen

packages.name: Wl-clipboard
packages.description: Copy and paste from the terminal on Wayland (wl-copy and wl-paste).
packages.why: Without it, scripts and the terminal cannot use the clipboard on Wayland.
packages.highlight: Copy and paste from scripts on Wayland

packages.name: Brightnessctl
packages.description: Change the screen brightness from the terminal or with a key.
packages.why: Makes the brightness keys of your laptop work on a tiling window manager.
packages.highlight: Makes the brightness keys work

packages.name: Playerctl
packages.description: Control music players (play, pause, next) from the terminal.
packages.why: Lets the media keys and your bar control Spotify, VLC and others.
packages.highlight: One command controls every player

packages.name: Lightdm
packages.description: A light login screen that works with many desktops.
packages.why: Pick it if you want a simple login screen with any window manager.
packages.highlight: Login screen that works with any desktop

packages.name: Sddm
packages.description: The login screen of KDE Plasma, with many themes.
packages.why: Easy to theme, and it can start both X11 and Wayland sessions.
packages.highlight: Themeable login screen of KDE

packages.name: Arandr
packages.description: A simple window to arrange your monitors on X11.
packages.why: Set the position of two screens by dragging them, then save it as a script.
packages.highlight: Drag your monitors into place

packages.name: Xclip
packages.description: Copy and paste from the terminal on X11.
packages.why: Many scripts and Neovim need it to use the system clipboard.
packages.highlight: Copy and paste from scripts on X11

packages.name: Maim
packages.description: A screenshot tool for X11.
packages.why: Fast and small, good with a key binding in i3 or BSPWM.
packages.highlight: Fast screenshots on X11

packages.name: Picom
packages.description: A compositor for X11 that adds transparency, shadows and rounded corners.
packages.why: You need it for blur and nice looking windows on i3 or BSPWM.
packages.highlight: Shadows, blur and transparency on X11

packages.name: Nitrogen
packages.description: A small program to set the wallpaper on X11.
packages.why: Pick a folder, click a picture, and it remembers your choice.
packages.highlight: Pick a wallpaper with a click

packages.name: Lxappearance
packages.description: A window to change the GTK theme, the icons and the cursor.
packages.why: The easiest way to theme GTK apps when you do not use a full desktop environment.
packages.highlight: Change GTK themes, icons and cursor

packages.name: Qt5ct
packages.description: A tool to set the theme of Qt apps outside KDE.
packages.why: Makes Qt apps like VLC and OBS match the rest of your desktop.
packages.highlight: Makes Qt apps match your theme

packages.name: Papirus Icons
packages.description: A popular icon theme with clean flat icons.
packages.why: It replaces the plain icons and makes your desktop look finished in a minute.
packages.highlight: Thousands of matching flat icons

packages.name: Cava
packages.description: A music visualizer that draws bars in the terminal.
packages.why: A classic for ricing screenshots, it reacts to the music you play.
packages.highlight: Music bars that dance in the terminal

packages.name: Cmatrix
packages.description: The falling green letters from the Matrix movie, in your terminal.
packages.why: It does nothing useful, but it is a fun part of a ricing screenshot.
packages.highlight: The Matrix rain in your terminal

packages.name: Starship
packages.description: A fast prompt for any shell that shows the git branch, the language and more.
packages.why: One line in your config gives you a modern prompt in Zsh, Fish or Bash.
packages.highlight: Pretty prompt for every shell

packages.name: Zoxide
packages.description: A smarter cd command that remembers the folders you use.
packages.why: After a few days, typing z and a part of the name jumps to the right folder.
packages.highlight: cd that remembers where you go

packages.name: Bat
packages.description: Like cat, but with colors and line numbers.
packages.why: Makes reading files in the terminal much nicer.
packages.highlight: cat with colors and line numbers

packages.name: Eza
packages.description: A modern ls with colors, icons and a tree view.
packages.why: A better looking ls for almost no effort.
packages.highlight: ls with icons, colors and git status

packages.name: Jq
packages.description: A tool to read and filter JSON in the terminal.
packages.why: Very useful when you work with APIs, like your json-server.
packages.highlight: Filter and pretty print JSON

packages.name: Htop
packages.description: A colorful view of the running programs and the memory they use.
packages.why: Lets you see what makes your computer slow and close it.
packages.highlight: See and stop what slows your PC

packages.name: Ncdu
packages.description: Shows which folders use the most disk space.
packages.why: Find in seconds what filled your disk.
packages.highlight: Find what filled your disk

packages.name: Tree
packages.description: Prints the folders and files as a tree.
packages.why: Good to show the structure of a project.
packages.highlight: See a folder as a tree

packages.name: Ranger
packages.description: A file manager for the terminal with Vim keys.
packages.why: Quick file browsing with previews and no mouse.
packages.highlight: Browse files with Vim keys

packages.name: Midnight Commander
packages.description: A file manager in the terminal with two panels.
packages.why: Copy and move files between two folders easily, even over SSH.
packages.highlight: Two panels, copy files in a second

packages.name: Lazygit
packages.description: A terminal screen for Git: stage, commit and push with a few keys.
packages.why: Faster than typing git commands once you learn the keys.
packages.highlight: Git with menus in the terminal

packages.name: Zellij
packages.description: A terminal workspace like Tmux, with menus that show the keys.
packages.why: Easier to learn than Tmux because the keys are shown on the screen.
packages.highlight: Tmux, but it shows you the keys

packages.name: Screen
packages.description: Keeps programs running after you close the terminal.
packages.why: Useful when you work on a server through SSH.
packages.highlight: Keep a program running over SSH

packages.name: Terminator
packages.description: A terminal that splits the window into many panels.
packages.why: Good for people who need many terminals at once and do not use tiling.
packages.highlight: Split one window into many terminals

packages.name: Tilix
packages.description: A tiling terminal for GNOME with many panels.
packages.why: Splits the window in panels and has a clean look.
packages.highlight: Tiling terminal for GNOME

packages.name: Xterm
packages.description: The oldest terminal for X11, very small.
packages.why: It always works, even on a broken system.
packages.highlight: Works on every X11 system

packages.name: Ghostty
packages.description: A fast terminal that draws with the graphics card and has simple settings.
packages.why: One config file, good defaults and a modern look.
packages.highlight: Native, fast and simple to set up

packages.name: Tldr
packages.description: Short examples for commands, instead of the long manual.
packages.why: Type tldr tar and see the three commands you really need.
packages.highlight: Examples instead of long manuals

packages.name: Duf
packages.description: A nicer view of your disks and how full they are.
packages.why: Easier to read than the df command.
packages.highlight: Disk usage you can read at a glance

packages.name: GNOME Terminal
packages.description: The default terminal of GNOME with tabs and profiles.
packages.why: Simple and stable if you do not need anything fancy.
packages.highlight: Profiles and tabs, works out of the box

packages.name: Konsole
packages.description: The terminal of KDE Plasma with tabs and split view.
packages.why: Many settings are in menus, so you do not have to edit files.
packages.highlight: Tabs, splits and profiles for KDE

packages.name: Nautilus
packages.description: The file manager of GNOME, simple and clean.
packages.why: Easy to use and a good default if you use GNOME.
packages.highlight: Clean and simple, the GNOME way

packages.name: Dolphin
packages.description: The file manager of KDE with tabs, split view and many features.
packages.why: The most powerful graphical file manager on Linux.
packages.highlight: Tabs, split view and a terminal panel

packages.name: Nemo
packages.description: The file manager of Linux Mint, similar to Windows Explorer.
packages.why: Familiar if you come from Windows.
packages.highlight: Windows Explorer feeling

packages.name: PCManFM
packages.description: A very light file manager.
packages.why: Good for old computers and for window managers.
packages.highlight: Runs on very old computers

packages.name: File Roller
packages.description: Open and create zip, tar and other archives with a window.
packages.why: Lets you open any archive without the terminal.
packages.highlight: Open any archive with a double click

packages.name: GNOME Calculator
packages.description: A simple calculator with a scientific mode.
packages.why: A quick calculator that does not need a browser.
packages.highlight: Scientific mode and currency converter

packages.name: Mousepad
packages.description: A simple text editor, like Notepad.
packages.why: Opens fast when you only need to change a small file.
packages.highlight: Notepad for Linux

packages.name: Flameshot
packages.description: A screenshot tool where you can draw arrows and text on the picture.
packages.why: The easiest screenshot tool for a beginner.
packages.highlight: Draw arrows and text on a screenshot

packages.name: Wget
packages.description: Download files from the terminal.
packages.why: Many install guides use it.
packages.highlight: Downloads that can resume

packages.name: Rsync
packages.description: Copy folders fast and send only what changed.
packages.why: The best tool for backups to a USB drive or a server.
packages.highlight: Copies only what changed

packages.name: Unzip
packages.description: Open zip files from the terminal.
packages.why: Small, but you will need it sooner or later.
packages.highlight: Opens zip files

packages.name: Zip
packages.description: Create zip files from the terminal.
packages.why: Lets you send a folder as one file.
packages.highlight: Makes zip files

packages.name: Bash Completion
packages.description: Press Tab to complete commands and options in Bash.
packages.why: Saves you a lot of typing.
packages.highlight: Tab completes options too

packages.name: TLP
packages.description: Saves laptop battery by itself, with almost no setup.
packages.why: Install it, enable it, and your battery lasts longer.
packages.highlight: Longer battery life with no setup

packages.name: Powertop
packages.description: Shows which programs use the most battery power.
packages.why: Helps you find what drains your laptop.
packages.highlight: Shows what drains the battery

packages.name: CUPS
packages.description: The printing system of Linux.
packages.why: You need it to use a printer.
packages.highlight: Makes printers work

packages.name: Pavucontrol
packages.description: A window to control the volume of each app and the sound devices.
packages.why: Fixes most sound problems on a window manager.
packages.highlight: Volume for every app on its own

packages.name: Blueman
packages.description: A Bluetooth manager with a tray icon.
packages.why: Connect headphones and a mouse without the terminal.
packages.highlight: Bluetooth from the tray

packages.name: GNOME Disks
packages.description: See your disks, check their health and write USB sticks.
packages.why: A simple way to see what is on every disk.
packages.highlight: Check disks and write USB sticks

packages.name: GParted
packages.description: Create and resize disk partitions with a window.
packages.why: The safest way to prepare a disk, for example for dual boot.
packages.highlight: Resize partitions safely

packages.name: Inxi
packages.description: Prints a summary of your hardware and system.
packages.why: Good to copy when you ask for help in a forum.
packages.highlight: Your whole system in one text

packages.name: Nvtop
packages.description: Like htop, but for the graphics card.
packages.why: Shows how much the GPU is used by a game or a program.
packages.highlight: htop for your graphics card

packages.name: Smartmontools
packages.description: Checks if your SSD or hard disk is healthy.
packages.why: Warns you before a disk dies.
packages.highlight: Warns you before a disk dies

packages.name: Visual Studio Code
packages.description: The most used code editor, with thousands of extensions.
packages.why: Great for web development and for your React course.
packages.highlight: Thousands of extensions, great for web

packages.name: VSCodium
packages.description: VS Code built without the Microsoft tracking and branding.
packages.why: The same editor, but fully open source.
packages.highlight: VS Code without telemetry

packages.name: IntelliJ IDEA
packages.description: The free Community edition of the JetBrains IDE for Java.
